chunks: From him, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: When a man intends divorce, he divorces her before the expiration of her waiting period without sexual intercourse. If he divorces her once and then leaves her until her waiting period expires, if he wishes to court her along with other suitors, he may do so. If he revokes her before the waiting period expires or after it, she is still considered his with one divorce. If he divorces her a second time and wishes to court her along with other suitors, provided he left her until the waiting period expired, and if he wishes, he may revoke her before the waiting period expires; if he does so, she is with him with two divorces. If he divorces her a third time, she does not become permissible to him until she marries another husband, and she inherits and is inherited from as she was in the blood-relationship of the first two divorces.
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for a husband to remarry his wife after a revocable divorce without consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar elucidates the procedural distinctions between revocable (raj'i) and irrevocable (ba'in) divorces, emphasizing that remarriage during the 'iddah requires a new marriage contract (nikah) rather than simple reversion. It highlights the unique Shia perspective on inheritance rights persisting during the interim period and the condition of 'tanzil' (returning to the original state) before the final third divorce renders the wife permanently unlawful until a subsequent marriage.
